transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… well, work kind of made me come in. I wait tables, and things got weird during service. Like, I’d just freeze in the middle of the floor, or I’d do things in the wrong order.

One night I was just standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key and saying table numbers over and over instead of closing the checks. And the soda station is already always sticky, you know, like no one cleans the nozzles right… but everyone was staring at me, and I guess it scared them. So… yeah, that’s why I’m here.
During that episode by the soda station, do you remember what was happening at the time, or does it feel like a blank—like you can't recall that part at all?

I remember pieces of it. I don’t think it was totally blank. I was by the soda station, and I had the cash drawer key in my hand, but I wasn’t doing what I was supposed to do, like closing out the checks. I just kept saying table numbers… like over and over.

And it’s stupid, because I kept thinking the soda nozzles were sticky and someone should clean them, but then I wasn’t moving. I was just kind of stuck there while service was going on, and I guess that’s what scared everybody.
When you were stuck by the soda station saying the table numbers, about how long did that whole episode last—was it just a few seconds, a couple of minutes, or longer?

I’m not totally sure how long… it felt longer than it probably was. I mean, service time gets strange because everything is timed by tables and tickets and who needs refills, and the soda station is right there with the sticky nozzles, so I remember thinking about that.

But I wasn’t just pausing for a second. I was standing there holding the cash drawer key, saying the table numbers over and over instead of closing checks. Long enough that people noticed and got scared, I guess. Maybe a couple minutes? I don’t know exactly.
In the hours before this episode happened, had you used any alcohol, drugs, or new medications?

I don’t know… I mean, I wasn’t really thinking about that before it happened. I was just trying to get through the shift, and it was busy, and the tickets were all backed up—like when the kitchen printer makes that noise and everyone acts like it’s personally your fault.

I don’t remember taking anything new right before, if that’s what you mean. Alcohol or drugs… I mean, I don’t think so? I was at work, so… no, not like that. I just remember being there and things getting kind of mixed up.
Have you ever had an episode like this before—losing track of what you were doing or saying something over and over—at any other point in your life?

I mean… not exactly like that, but I guess there have been times where I kind of lose the thread of what I’m supposed to be doing. At work it’s worse because everything is happening at once, and people are asking for ranch or refills and the kitchen is yelling for runners, and then suddenly I’m doing the wrong part first.

That time by the soda station is the one everyone keeps talking about because I froze up in the middle of service. I had the cash drawer key and I should’ve been closing checks, but instead I was just standing there saying table numbers over and over. It’s embarrassing. Like, I knew there was a thing I was supposed to do, but it got out of order in my head.
After that episode by the soda station ended, how did you feel—did you feel confused, very tired, or unable to remember what had just happened, or did you feel back to normal fairly quickly?

I don’t know if I felt “normal” right away. I remember people looking at me like I’d done something really wrong, and that made it worse. The soda station is so cramped too, with everyone reaching around you for ice and lids, and I was just there with the cash drawer key in my hand.

What scared them, I think, was more that I wasn’t doing the next thing. I was supposed to be closing checks, but I got stuck saying the table numbers, like they were the order of things, and I couldn’t get it lined up. Afterward I felt embarrassed and kind of scrambled, not like I smoothly snapped back.
Right before you found yourself stuck at the soda station, did you notice any warning signs—like a strange smell, taste, tingling, or a sudden odd feeling—just before it started?

I don’t really remember anything like that… not a smell or taste or tingling. I mean, the soda station always smells like syrup and bleach and wet towels, so it’s hard to say what counts as “strange,” you know?

I mostly remember being in the middle of everything and trying to keep the table numbers straight, and then it was like I got stuck on them. If there was a warning feeling before it, I didn’t notice it.
During that episode, did you bite your tongue, lose control of your bladder, or get hurt in any way—like falling or bumping into something?

I don’t think so… nobody told me I fell or anything. I was just standing there, which is part of why it felt so stupid, like if I’d tripped at least people would know what to do, you know?

I don’t remember biting my tongue. And I didn’t… I mean, I don’t think I lost control of my bladder. My apron was sticky from soda stuff already, because the station is always a mess, but not like that. I don’t remember being hurt, just embarrassed with everyone staring.

Have you or anyone else noticed other episodes—like brief staring spells, lip-smacking, hand fumbling, or repetitive movements—happening at other times, even small ones you might not have thought were connected to this?

I don’t know about lip-smacking or anything like that. Nobody’s said it that way to me.

What they do notice is more like… I freeze up in the middle of service, or I’ll do things in the wrong order. Like that time I was just standing by the soda station with the cash drawer key in my hand, repeating table numbers instead of closing the checks. And then everyone’s waiting on me, and the drinks are backing up, and somebody needs ranch or extra lemons—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

It’s not like a little habit I’m aware of. It’s more that I get stuck, and people get scared because I’m not doing what I’m supposed to be doing.

Looking back at the times this has happened, do the episodes tend to occur during moments that feel especially stressful or overwhelming to you, or do they seem to happen randomly, even during calm moments?

It’s usually when it’s busy, I think… like during service, when everybody needs something and the tickets are stacking up. But then, restaurants are always kind of stressful, even when people say it’s a “calm” shift, because there’s still someone asking for more ice or the soda syrup is out or the drawer won’t close right.

What scared everyone was that I’d just freeze in the middle of it, or do things all wrong. Like I was standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, saying table numbers over and over, instead of closing the checks like I was supposed to. So… I guess it happens more when I’m overwhelmed, but it doesn’t feel like I choose it or see it coming.
Has this kind of freezing or getting stuck ever happened when you were relaxed, at home, or not under any pressure at all—like while watching TV or just sitting quietly?

I mean… I’m trying to think. At home it’s different, because if I stop doing something nobody’s yelling for drinks or waiting on checks, so it doesn’t feel as obvious.

The thing everyone got scared about was at work, during service. I’d freeze up or do stuff in the wrong order—like I was by the soda station holding the cash drawer key and just saying table numbers over and over, instead of closing the checks. That’s the one people keep bringing up.

At home… I don’t know. I sit there sometimes and lose track of what I was doing, but it’s not like there’s a manager staring at me or the whole section getting backed up, so I don’t notice it the same way.
Has anyone ever noticed you having an episode like this while you were asleep or just waking up—such as unusual movements, confusion, or biting your tongue during the night?

I don’t think so… I mean, nobody’s told me that. I live alone, so unless I woke up with something obvious, I don’t know how I’d know.

Sometimes I wake up confused, but I think everybody does if the alarm goes off wrong or you fall asleep with the TV on and it’s some weird infomercial yelling about cookware. I haven’t noticed anything like biting my tongue, though… or someone saying I was moving strange in my sleep. There’s not really anyone there watching me sleep, you know?

Can you think of a specific time at home, when you were completely calm and not focused on any task, where you noticed yourself suddenly freezing up or losing track of what you were doing, even briefly?

At home, I can’t think of a clear time like that where I was just totally calm and then froze. It’s harder to tell there, because if I lose the thread of something, there isn’t a whole dining room waiting on me, you know?

The specific thing that keeps coming back is work. Like, during service I’d just stop in the middle of everything or do it in the wrong order. I was by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I kept saying table numbers instead of closing out checks. And then people were looking at me like, “What are you doing?” That’s the one that scared everybody.
During that episode, did anyone try to touch you, call your name, or get your attention—and if so, did that seem to change what you were doing or bring you out of it?

I think they were saying my name, yeah… or at least people were talking at me, because it was service and everyone talks over each other. But the part everyone remembers is I was just standing there by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I kept saying table numbers, like that was going to help, instead of closing the checks.

I don’t know if someone touching me changed it exactly. It was more like once people started looking at me and asking what I was doing, I sort of realized I wasn’t doing the thing I was supposed to be doing. But it wasn’t like a clean snap-out-of-it. I was embarrassed, mostly. And then of course the whole section was backed up, and that’s when managers get that face, you know, like you’ve personally ruined iced tea for the entire building.

When these freezing or 'stuck' episodes happen, do they tend to look the same every time—same kind of movements or words, lasting about the same length of time—or does what happens and how long it lasts change depending on the situation?

It’s not exactly like… a perfect repeat every time, I don’t think. It depends on what’s going on around me. At work it was mostly that I’d just stop in the middle of service or do things in the wrong order.

Like the soda station thing—standing there with the cash drawer key, saying table numbers over and over instead of closing out checks. That’s the one people got scared about, because it looked so wrong, I guess. I don’t know if it’s always the same length of time. When you’re in the middle of a rush, thirty seconds feels like somebody left you in a room for an hour, you know?

During that episode at the soda station, if someone had asked you a direct question—like 'What's your name?' or 'What are you doing?'—do you think you would have been able to understand and answer them appropriately, or does it feel like you wouldn't have been able to respond at all?

I don’t know if I would’ve answered right away. Maybe if someone said my name really sharply, I would’ve kind of looked up, but the scary part was more that I was just… doing the wrong thing and not catching it.

Like I was standing there by the soda station with the cash drawer key in my hand, and instead of closing checks I kept saying table numbers, like that was somehow the next step. It sounds stupid when I say it. Restaurants are already chaotic, and the soda machine makes that hissing noise, and people are asking for ranch and refills and everything, so maybe I heard them, but I wasn’t putting it together right.

If someone asked, “What are you doing?” I think I probably would’ve been embarrassed and confused, not totally gone. But I wasn’t acting normal. I was frozen up in the middle of service, doing things out of order, and that’s what freaked everybody out.
Setting aside the soda station incident, how many separate times would you say you've had this kind of freezing or getting 'stuck' episode in the past, and over what period of time did they occur?

I mean… I don’t have a clean number, because it wasn’t like I was keeping a little tally on a napkin or something. The soda station one is the one everybody brings up because it was so obvious, me just standing there with the cash drawer key and repeating table numbers instead of closing checks.

But there were other times at work where I’d freeze in the middle of service, or I’d start doing things in the wrong order and someone would have to kind of steer me back. I’d be at a table or near the POS and suddenly I’m not doing the next step. It was over that stretch when things were getting bad at work, not like one single day.

I know that’s not a great answer. It’s just… restaurant time is weird. Everything is loud and fast and then later people act like you should remember exactly how many times you looked stupid in front of the whole dinner rush.
During that episode at the soda station, were your eyes open or closed, and if someone tried to open your eyelids, do you know if you resisted or kept them shut?

I… I don’t really know about my eyelids. I wasn’t thinking, “Are my eyes open?” in that moment. People mostly talked about how I was just standing there by the soda station with the cash drawer key, repeating table numbers instead of closing checks, like my brain had skipped to the wrong page.

I don’t remember anyone trying to open my eyes or anything like that. It wasn’t like that’s what scared them. It was more me freezing in the middle of service and doing everything out of order, and then the whole station is backing up and everybody’s staring.

During these freezing episodes, have you or others noticed your hands doing any small repetitive movements—like fumbling with objects, picking at your clothes, or fidgeting—that you weren't aware of at the time?

I don’t know about little hand movements, exactly. Nobody said, like, “you were picking at your shirt” or anything. What people noticed was more the bigger thing—me freezing up in the middle of service and doing stuff in the wrong order.

Like at the soda station, I had the cash drawer key in my hand, and I was just standing there repeating table numbers instead of closing checks. Which is ridiculous, because I know how to close checks, I’ve done it a million times. And then the drinks are backing up, the machine’s making noise, servers are trying to get around you, and suddenly you’re the problem in everybody’s way.

So… if I was fumbling with the key, maybe, but I don’t remember it that way. The scary part everyone talked about was me getting stuck and not moving through the steps like I was supposed to.
During these episodes, do you ever feel detached from yourself or your surroundings, like you're watching yourself from outside your body or like things aren't quite real?

I’m not sure. I don’t really remember it like floating above myself or anything that clear. It’s more like… I know I’m there, but then I’m not doing the next thing I’m supposed to do, and everybody else seems to know before I do that something’s off.

The “things aren’t real” part is hard, because restaurants already feel unreal sometimes, you know? The lights, the noise, the same orders over and over, people yelling “behind” and “corner,” and then someone wants ranch like it’s an emergency. So I don’t know if that’s detached or just being overwhelmed.

I haven’t noticed myself watching from outside my body, no. I just kind of get stuck, and then afterward people tell me what it looked like.
